As far as I can tell, ArtCraft currently only operates with cloud-provided generation services. I've already set up local generation via ComfyUI, and it would be great to be able to hook into that. In terms of actually getting it working, I think I would break it into three parts. First, the adapter that would send the information from the GUI to the local service. title: Feature Request: An Adobe Encore Alternative for DVD/Blu-ray Authoring
author: renji-toda
body:
I would like to suggest a future ArtCraft application for **DVD-Video and Blu-ray authoring**, as a modern alternative to Adobe Encore.

Adobe Encore CS6 is still one of the best tools I have found for creating highly customized DVD/Blu-ray menus, but it has been discontinued for many years. Unfortunately, most modern alternatives sacrifice creative freedom for template-based menus.

What I am looking for is not simply software that can "burn a DVD/Blu-ray", but an authoring tool where the creator can **design the entire menu and then define its behavior**.

### Key features

* DVD-Video and Blu-ray authoring
* DVD ISO and Blu-ray ISO output
* Import custom menu backgrounds
* Import custom button artwork
* Freely position buttons
* Assign arbitrary navigation links to buttons
* Button highlight states
* Separate main/title menus and chapter/scene menus
* Multiple levels of menu navigation
* Still-image, video, and audio menu backgrounds
* Chapter/scene selection
* Ideally, one project that can produce both DVD and Blu-ray versions

The most important principle would be:

> **The software should provide the authoring engine, while the creator controls the design.**

In other words, the user should not be restricted to predefined menu templates. A menu designed in Photoshop or another graphics application should be usable essentially as designed, with author-defined interactive areas and navigation.

I believe there is still a real need for this. Adobe Encore and DVD Architect demonstrated that there is a market for highly customizable disc authoring, but both are now discontinued. Most current consumer tools can create DVDs and Blu-rays, but their menu systems are considerably more restrictive.

This seems like a natural fit for the philosophy behind ArtCraft: a modern, user-controlled alternative to a discontinued professional creative tool.

I would personally love to see an **"Encore-like" DiscCraft / AuthorCraft** become part of the ArtCraft family.

title: [Bug] Denied task-queue localStorage read prevents the frontend from mounting
author: Jagalite
body:
Rejecting one optional task-queue localStorage read makes the production frontend render a blank screen before account setup. Restoring that read and reloading restores the normal account-creation screen.

## Environment

- Current main `3e5793b6934b51536606720e5d56bcfd1fe7cc2d`, rechecked on 2026-10-07; unchanged from the tested locked production Vite build.
- macOS 26.5.2 arm64, Apple M1; isolated standalone Chrome 154.0.8037.93, Firefox 155.0 and Playwright WebKit 26.6 (not Safari), headless, frontend hosted at a loopback root.
- Standalone production frontend only. No mocked Tauri bridge, test account, provider calls or packaged-WebView qualification.

## Reproduction

1. Before the frontend entry mounts, wrap `Storage.prototype.getItem` to throw `new DOMException("Generated task queue read denial", "SecurityError")` only when the receiver is `localStorage` and the key is `taskQueueLastReadAt`. Delegate every other read to the original implementation.
2. Load the production frontend and wait four seconds after DOM readiness. Inspect the visible page and `#root.childElementCount`; capture uncaught errors and the intercepted key.
3. Disable the fault and reload the same isolated page. Inspect the root and visible screen again.
4. Repeat in a clean context without the fault as a baseline.

All three engines reproduce:

- The optional key is read twice; both reads are rejected.
- The React root has zero children and the screen is blank. An uncaught SecurityError is recorded.
- Restoring the single read and reloading gives two root children and the ordinary account-creation UI. Clean no-fault controls reach the same account UI.
- The failure occurs before an authenticated viewer or provider scenario is needed.

Treat an unavailable last-read timestamp as absent/default and allow the frontend to mount. An optional task-queue preference should not replace the entire application with a blank screen.

title: Strategic Growth: Capturing the Massive Indian Market with Native Indic language Support
author: Alisowetto
body:
Hi Brandon and the team! I'm a designer from India, and I've been following the ArtCraft suite with a lot of excitement. To be completely honest, the #1 reason I'm looking for an alternative is that I refuse to pay Adobe's massive subscription fees—they are completely out of line with local earnings here. 

Right now, millions of Indian designers and students are forced to use buggy, unsafe, pirated versions of Photoshop and Illustrator because we don't have a choice. We want a clean, legal, lightweight alternative, but there is one massive roadblock keeping us from switching to ArtCraft: lack of native Indic language support (like Bengali, Hindi, etc.).

Because Indic scripts are complex, typing Bengali in the current text engine breaks the letters apart—conjunct clusters fail to merge, and vowel markers (matras) sit on the wrong side. 

If VectorCraft, PhotoCraft, and DesignCraft can integrate a proper complex text-shaping engine (like HarfBuzz), you will instantly solve a problem for millions of Indian creators. title: You are asking for lawsuits
author: CHJ85
body:
You guys need to walk a lot more careful. The phrasing—flaunting **"clean-room reimplementation of Adobe Photoshop/Illustrator"** right there in the repository headers—is essentially waving a red cape in front of a corporate bull.

To a layperson, saying "we rewrote Photoshop from scratch" sounds like a legal safe-harbor keyword. To an intellectual property lawyer, it looks like a neon sign blinking: *"Please look closely at our codebase and how it was made."*

Using the term "clean-room" is a calculated legal defense, but putting it front and center in a repository description while cloning a multi-billion-dollar corporation's product line creates massive vulnerabilities for a few reasons:

### 1. The Paradox of the "Clean-Room" Claim

A true legal clean-room design requires a strict, verifiable firewall:

* Team A analyzes Adobe's software behavior and writes *functional specifications* (what the software should do, without looking at the underlying code).
* Team B (who has never seen Adobe's code *or* reverse-engineered it) writes the actual code based strictly on Team A's specs.

When an individual developer "vibe-codes" an entire application suite using an LLM (like Claude), the clean-room defense gets very murky. LLMs are trained on massive swathes of internet data, documentation, and potentially open-source code repositories that touch file formats, rendering logic, and algorithms. If Adobe’s legal team subpoenas the developer or forces discovery on how the code was generated, proving a pristine, legally bulletproof clean-room process becomes an uphill battle.

### 2. Trademark and Trade Dress Aggression

Even if Adobe can't easily sue over pure functionality or standard UI layouts (since tools like Photopea have danced around this line for years), they don't have to limit themselves to copyright.

title: Custom theme from a file: let the desktop supply ArtCraft's colors
author: NobleDoodle
body:
ArtCraft's colors are already CSS variables (`--st-bg`, `--st-panel`, `--st-fg`, `--background`, `--primary`, … in `frontend/apps/artcraft/app/src/styles/base.css`), switched by the `theme-*` class that `st-theme` selects. That's an ideal shape for desktop theming tools (Omarchy's palette, pywal, base16), but nothing outside the app can reach those variables today, so the only option is picking one of the five built-in themes.

**Proposal**

- A "Custom" theme whose colors come from `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ai.artcraft.app/theme.json`, or the shared `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/craft/theme.json` proposed for the Crafting Apps in storytold/photocraft#2120, re-read when the file changes.
- The same shared names (`background`, `surface`, `border`, `text`, `textDim`, `accent`, `accentText`, `danger`, `warning`) mapped onto ArtCraft's variables, so one file themes ArtCraft and the Crafting Apps alike.
- `#rrggbb` values only, applied with `style.setProperty`, never as raw CSS; unknown keys ignored.
- Optionally a "System" choice that follows `prefers-color-scheme` between the light theme and a dark one.

I'm happy to help with a PR if this direction works for you.

body:
Notes from a performance pass over the desktop app. The small fixes are in a separate PR; these need a maintainer's call, so I am raising them rather than changing them.

## 1. The entry JS chunk is 6.5 MB

`npx vite build` in `frontend/apps/artcraft` produces:

| Chunk                          | Size      |
|--------------------------------|-----------|
| `index-*.js` (entry)           | 6,502 kB  |
| `index-*.js` (second)          | 1,586 kB  |
| `index-*.js` (contains ammo)   | 422 kB    |
| `opencut_wasm_bg-*.wasm`       | 3,038 kB  |

The entry chunk contains three.js, the Spark splat renderer, Konva, PostHog and zip.js, so they are parsed on every launch even though `MainApp.tsx` lazy-loads its pages. Something on the eager import path (probably a barrel `index.ts` or a shared store) pulls them in. `vite.config.ts` has no `manualChunks`. I have not timed startup, only measured the output size.

## 2. `list_tasks_for_frontend` returns every non-dismissed task, every 5 seconds

`crates/schema/database/sqlite_tasks/src/queries/list_tasks_for_frontend.rs` has no `LIMIT` and filters only on `is_dismissed_by_user`, which has no index. Completed tasks are never auto-dismissed, so the result grows with history. Two components poll it on separate 5s timers (`TopBar/TaskQueue.tsx` and `generation-feed/useDesktopGenerationFeed.ts`) and then discard most rows client-side. Currently, only the x64 Windows installer is provided in Releases. While the x64 binary can run under Windows 11 emulation (Prism), a native ARM64 build would:
- Deliver significantly better CPU efficiency and lower memory footprint.
- Maximize battery life on portable ARM laptops.
- Take full advantage of native WebView2 and Rust runtime performance without emulation overhead.

### Proposed Solution
Since ArtCraft is built with Tauri and Rust, adding Windows ARM64 support is straightforward via cross-compilation on GitHub Actions (`windows-latest` runner)

title: Stylus input broken in all Linux desktop apps and the Launcher (Wayland): cursor moves, clicks don't registe
author: SArneitzUni
body:
Environment:

    Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, GNOME on Wayland
    MSI Prestige 16 AI+ Flip (built-in pen display/digitizer)
    Apps (all latest versions) installed via  ArtCraft Launcher (craft-launcher v0.2.0).

Description:
The stylus cannot be used inside the apps and the main launcher. The pen moves the cursor inside the app window, but clicks/presses do not register at all — no drawing, no UI interaction with the pen. Touch and mouse work normally.

Diagnostics:

-     The app runs as a native Wayland client (does not appear in xlsclients while running).
-     No warnings or errors in terminal output when touching pen to screen.
-     The pen works correctly in other native Wayland apps (Firefox, GNOME Settings) and in Qt apps forced to Wayland (QT_QPA_PLATFORM=wayland krita).
-     The pen works in the WebAssembly/browser version of the app, so canvas input handling works — the issue is specific to the desktop input stack.

Likely cause: On Wayland, stylus events are delivered via the zwp_tablet_v2 protocol, not as wl_pointer events. The desktop app appears to only handle pointer events, so pen motion moves the cursor (compositor-side) but pen-down never reaches the app. Handling tablet-tool events (or synthesizing pointer clicks from pen contact) would fix this. For a drawing-focused tool, full pressure support via the tablet protocol would also be very welcome.

author: charles-hood
body:
## The gap

Of the Office family, Word, Excel and PowerPoint now have Craft apps. Visio does not, and it is the one Microsoft sells separately: Visio Plan 1 and Plan 2 are their own subscriptions on top of Microsoft 365, with the desktop app only on Plan 2. The people who need it (network and datacenter engineers, systems architects, process and compliance teams, anyone drawing an org chart or a floor plan) tend to be exactly the people who were told "we don't pay for Visio here" and ended up drawing boxes in PowerPoint instead.

title: [App Request] CADCraft – 3D CAD, CAM & mechanical design (Autodesk Fusion 360 alternative)
author: mateowoetam
body:
**Problem / Context**
Artists, makers, and hardware designers using the Craft ecosystem currently lack an integrated parametric 3D CAD and CAM workspace for mechanical design, assembly modeling, and manufacturing preparation, forcing them to jump to proprietary cloud-locked tools like Autodesk Fusion 360.

**Proposed Solution**
Introduce **CADCraft**, a focused app within the Craft ecosystem tailored for precise 3D parametric modeling, mechanical assemblies, sheet metal design, and CAM toolpath generation, keeping workflow state locally inside `.craft` project files.

**Key Features**
* **Parametric Sketching & Modeling:** Dimension-driven 2D sketches mapped to robust 3D features, lofts, sweeps, and fillets.
* **Assembly Constraints:** Component mating, joints, and motion links to test mechanical mechanisms.
* **CAM & Toolpaths:** Basic 2.5axis and 3axis CNC milling simulations, G-code generation, and 3D printing preparation.
* **Blender & Mesh Bridge:** Clean conversion tools to transition precise CAD NURBS/BREP data into organic meshes for texture and render apps.

title: [App Request] MapCraft – open GIS and map design (ArcGIS alternative, publishes to GeoServer)
author: matbrgz
body:
[![Status: Proposed](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-proposed-blue.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Type: App Request](https://img.shields.io/badge/type-app_request-blueviolet.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Ecosystem: Artcraft](https://img.shields.io/badge/ecosystem-artcraft-8A2BE2.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Language: Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-Rust-DEA584.svg?style=flat-square&logo=rust)](https://www.rust-lang.org)

## ELI5
A map maker. Load places, roads, rivers or your own data, style them beautifully, and export a map for print, the web or a 3D scene. Like ArcGIS, but open and on your computer.

## What it does
- Open common geo data: GeoJSON, Shapefile, GeoPackage, GeoTIFF, KML, PMTiles
- Style maps visually (colors, labels, icons) and export to print/PDF, SVG or web tiles
- Terrain from elevation data → 3D scenes in ArtCraft ("put my scene in the real Alps")
- Publish a map as a web page or via standard OGC services (WMS/WFS)
- Built in Rust on georust/GDAL, with MapLibre for interactive maps

## Self-hosted option (available today)
- [GeoServer](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver) (GPL-2.0): the standard open server to publish maps and geo data (WMS, WFS, WMTS). Users can self-host it today and MapCraft can publish to it.
- [QGIS](https://github.com/qgis/QGIS) (GPL-2.0): mature open desktop GIS, a reference for features and formats.
- [MapLibre](https://github.com/maplibre/maplibre-gl-js) and [PMTiles](https://github.com/protomaps/PMTiles) (BSD-3): open web maps and single-file tiles, easy to embed.

## Motivation
- ArcGIS is expensive and closed; cities, NGOs and schools struggle to pay for it
- QGIS is powerful but hard for designers; there is no "beautiful maps" tool for creatives

title: Have you considered using REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) as a development tool?
author: JaredTweed
body:
Hi! I was wondering whether the ArtCraft team is already using, or has considered using, "REA (Reverse Engineer Anything)" (https://github.com/morluto/rea) during development.

REA is an open-source MCP toolkit that allows AI coding agents to investigate native applications, JavaScript/Electron apps, websites, and runtime behavior.

It seems like it could be useful for ArtCraft when researching how established creative tools implement particular features, such as:

- 2D compositing and image-editing behavior
- 3D scene manipulation and camera controls
- Image/video editing workflows and export behavior
- Complex interactions and edge cases that aren't well documented

It could potentially accelerate development by helping AI agents understand existing implementations and identify useful behavior to reproduce, while respecting licensing and clean-room development practices.

A couple of questions:

1. Is the team already using REA or a similar application-analysis tool?
2. If not, would it be worth experimenting with REA on a particular workflow to see whether it could improve development efficiency?

I'm suggesting it as an optional development tool rather than something that necessarily needs to be integrated into ArtCraft itself.

Thanks for considering it!

title: SQLite startup deletes task storage after any connection or migration error
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- rust-audit:d4e4ac69bbd93d237eaf5d0260bc6a5ff3a5e373:db-reset -->
## Assessment

**Severity:** High — conditional loss of local task history. **Confidence:** High in the source behavior; runtime/security preconditions are qualified below.

Found during an AI-assisted, read-only Rust audit of upstream main at [d4e4ac6](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft/commit/d4e4ac69bbd93d237eaf5d0260bc6a5ff3a5e373). No application exploits, authenticated provider requests, or destructive tests were performed. Rust/native runtime tests were not available; proposed tests below are not claimed as executed.

## Source evidence and root cause

- [`crates/schema/database/sqlite_tasks/src/connection.rs:14–61`](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft/blob/d4e4ac69bbd93d237eaf5d0260bc6a5ff3a5e373/crates/schema/database/sqlite_tasks/src/connection.rs#L14-L61)

`connect_and_migrate()` catches every error from `run_migrations()`, then calls `std::fs::remove_file(&database_file)` and retries. `run_migrations()` includes both opening the pool and running migrations; there is no error classification or backup.

## Trigger and realistic impact

A recoverable connection/locking or migration-checksum error can erase pending-job tracking and completion metadata when deletion succeeds. The database is intentionally described as ephemeral, but the reset applies more broadly than incompatible schemas. On Windows, outstanding handles may prevent deletion and leave startup failing instead.

## Recommended remediation

Preserve the original database on ordinary errors. Classify errors; close connections explicitly before any recovery. Quarantine/back up genuinely incompatible storage rather than unlinking it automatically; account for WAL sidecars and other app instances.

## Suggested regression tests

- Inject connection, lock and migration-checksum failures against disposable databases and assert rows survive.
- Separately test an explicitly approved reset path on Unix and Windows.
- Verify retry/…

## Assessment

**Severity:** High potential impact; historical key exposure NOT established. **Confidence:** High in the source behavior; runtime/security preconditions are qualified below.

Found during an AI-assisted, read-only Rust audit of upstream main at [d4e4ac6](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft/commit/d4e4ac69bbd93d237eaf5d0260bc6a5ff3a5e373). No application exploits, authenticated provider requests, or destructive tests were performed. Rust/native runtime tests were not available; proposed tests below are not claimed as executed.

author: vinnichase
body:
> *In the name of the -Craft name ancestor: StarCraft II.* 🫡

## Summary
Introduce an optional, position-based "grid" hotkey layout that works the same way in every ArtCraft app — modeled after the Grid hotkey preset in StarCraft II. The grid adapts to the current selection (like the command card for selected units), supports nested sub-grids so that sequences of keys ("key melodies", à la Vim) can reach a practically unlimited number of actions, and offers a mapping mode where users assign functions to grid cells simply by clicking them in the UI.

## How SC2 grid hotkeys work
- The command card is a 5×3 grid of buttons.
- Each grid cell is bound to a fixed key by **position**, not by mnemonic:
  Q W E R T
  A S D F G
  Z X C V B
- Whatever command sits in the top-left cell is always `Q`, regardless of its name. The left hand stays on the home row, and muscle memory carries over between units.
- The command card always shows the commands of the **currently selected units**.

## Proposal
1. Every app/tool context exposes its main actions as a visible grid panel (5×3).
2. Each cell maps to the corresponding key in the layout above.
3. A dedicated key (e.g. `Esc`) always means "back / cancel / up one level".
4. Common actions sit in the **same cell in every app** (e.g. select, move, delete, undo, export), so switching between apps doesn't require relearning.

title: Lottie-like animation support needed (open-source alternative to paid tools)
author: Adhishtanaka
body:
## Summary

ArtCraft needs a Lottie-like vector animation feature: lightweight, scalable, JSON-based animations that can be authored, previewed and exported inside the app.

## Motivation

Today the usual route for this kind of animation is a paid tool or service (for example After Effects with Bodymovin, or the paid tiers of LottieFiles). An open-source option built into ArtCraft would let artists, designers and filmmakers create and export these animations without a paid subscription.

## Proposal

- Build an open-source Lottie-compatible animation layer instead of depending on a paid product.
- Import and play existing Lottie (`.json` / `.lottie`) files.
- Do basic authoring: keyframes, shapes, paths, transforms and easing.
- Export to the Lottie JSON format so the output works with the existing players (web, iOS, Android).

## Possible open-source building blocks

- [lottie-web](https://github.com/airbnb/lottie-web) (MIT) for playback and rendering
- [ThorVG](https://github.com/thorvg/thorvg) (MIT) for a lightweight vector and Lottie renderer
- [Skottie / Skia](https://skia.org/docs/user/modules/skottie/) (BSD) for native Lottie rendering
- [rlottie](https://github.com/Samsung/rlottie) (MIT) for native playback

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Users can import and preview Lottie animations
- [ ] Users can create or edit simple vector animations
- [ ] Users can export valid Lottie JSON
- [ ] No paid or proprietary dependency is required

### Idea

Add a **read-only feedback bot** to the ArtCraft Discord that collects feature requests and bug reports from each app's channels (DeckCraft, WordCraft, PdfCraft, FilmCraft, PhotoCraft, …) and links them to that app's GitHub issues.

A lot of useful feedback is posted on Discord, but it scrolls away, gets repeated, and often never reaches the repository where the work is tracked. - Fewer duplicate issues, because requests are matched to existing ones first.

1. **Collect:** read messages in the feedback and bug channels of each app (needs the Message Content intent, only in the channels the team chooses).

title: Feature request: multi-language support (i18n) with drop-in translation files
author: Willemsel
body:
Summary
I’d like to use the ArtCraft apps in Dutch, and I’m willing to contribute the translation. Right now all UI text is hard-coded in English, so there’s no way to add other languages.

**Proposed design**

Built on a standard i18n library (e.g. react-i18next), which loads the JSON files and handles the fallback to English.
A translations/ folder with one JSON file per language.
The file name is the language name, written in that language: English.json, Nederlands.json, Deutsch.json, Français.json, etc.
On startup the app scans the folder and fills the Language dropdown (Settings → Appearance) with the file names. No list of languages is hard-coded.
Adding or improving a language is just adding or editing a JSON file. No code changes and no new release needed.
Missing keys fall back to English.json, so an incomplete translation never breaks the app.
The chosen language is saved and applies immediately. It is independent of the system language, because users don’t always want the app in their OS language.

**Sharing translations**

Users can import/upload a translation file in the app, and it appears in the dropdown right away.
Uploaded translations can be shared, so others can use them immediately without waiting for an update.
All submitted translation files are bundled with each new release, so every user gets all available languages automatically.
Users can add their own translations by placing a JSON file in the translations folder (admin rights may be needed).
Note: a translation that a user makes but doesn’t share could be overwritten by an update. This is an edge case, and sharing translations avoids it.

Applies to all apps
The same folder and the same switch can be used for every ArtCraft app and component.

Proven approach
I use exactly this setup in my own app (Sheet Optimizer), with five languages, and it works well.

Contribution
I’m happy to provide Nederlands.json and help with the implementation. Are you open to this approach?

title: Tauri desktop: isolate remote analytics scripts and restrict local-file asset scope
author: neumdan
body:
## Problem and impact

The Tauri desktop main page combines remote analytics script execution with broadly scoped local-file access. If an allowed script or another main-page JavaScript source is compromised, that code inherits the page's ability to read user-accessible local files, including plaintext provider credentials. This is a high-impact post-compromise boundary weakness; no independent drive-by entry point, provider compromise, or RCE is claimed.

## Verified release and method

title: Subject: Idea for ArtCraft: Camtasia's ergonomics for quick and simple video editing
author: letutorien13
body:
Hi Brandon,

Congratulations on the amazing work you've done on the ArtCraft suite!

For a long time now, I've been trying to run a video editing software I know very well on Linux, without success. That software is Camtasia.

I don't know if you're familiar with it, but for quick and simple videos, its ergonomics are unmatched compared to heavy pro editors like Premiere Pro (or FilmCraft):
1. **Interactive Canvas:** You move, resize, and arrange your video overlays directly with the mouse on screen, just like a PowerPoint slide.
2. **Hassle-free Timeline:** A single key to slice clips instantly, with clips auto-snapping together so you don't leave gaps.
3. **Zero complex settings:** No need to manage nodes, effect channels, or sequence settings just to make a clean edit.

The problem is that it's impossible to use it anywhere other than Windows and macOS, and paying $250 a year is a total dealbreaker for me.

Softwares like Premiere Pro (or FilmCraft) are great for heavy editing, but they quickly feel overly complex when you just want to do a quick edit without hassle. Creating a video editor based on an ergonomics as simple, fast, and smooth as Camtasia, but natively available on Linux, Windows, and Mac, would be awesome.

By the way, if you like the idea, it could for example be called *CamtaCraft* (with maybe a *CaptureCraft* module for recording) to go alongside *FilmCraft*.

Best regards,

title: Proposal: standalone apps with an optional shared workspace, consistent UX and InDesign workflow compatibility
author: random3jane
body:
What you’ve built already is impressive. For such an early alpha, DesignCraft is surprisingly responsive; launching it and opening IDML files feels considerably faster than InDesign on my Mac Studio M2 with 64 GB of RAM. I also appreciate the MCP integration and its potential for production automation.

I work in magazine layout, prepress, photography and retouching, with many years of Adobe experience. A few observations from that perspective:


**Breadth versus depth**

Everyone understandably wants their favourite application added. But trying to cover everything risks the same development hell that, in my view, Adobe has reached: doing everything and too often nothing properly.

I’m not qualified to set your priorities, but I wonder how much effort it makes sense to invest in areas already served extremely well by DaVinci Resolve.


**Standalone apps, shared workspace**

Following the discussion in #2242, could the architecture support both standalone applications and optional modules within one shared workspace?

Combining LightCraft and PhotoCraft seems particularly promising: a substantial photographic catalogue, RAW development and layered retouching, with coherent metadata, version management, batch processing and export. Users could install either application separately or use both together.

Resolve’s task-based pages are an interesting reference; photography, illustration and layout increasingly overlap within the same job. This need not delay the first production releases, but it may be worth allowing for architecturally now.

title: [Bug] Photocraft Frame Tool (K) creates an invisible Group Layer at MacOS
author: lariCFL
body:
When using the Frame Tool (K) in PhotoCraft to create an image placeholder, the frame is completely invisible on the canvas and cannot be resized or positioned via the Properties panel. Instead of behaving like a visual frame object, it is created as an empty Group Layer with Pass Through blend mode and a mask thumbnail, lacking any bounding box, stroke, or transform handles.

Expected Behavior

⚬ The frame should render a visible wireframe/outline (or "X" placeholder box) on the canvas with transform handles when selected.
⚬ The Properties panel should display the Transform section with Width, Height, X, and Y input fields, just like it does for a Smart Object layer.

Actual Behavior

⚬ No canvas rendering: The canvas remains 100% transparent/blank with no visual indicator of where the frame was drawn (Cmd + T and Cmd + H do not reveal any box).
⚬ Only visible via Move Tool (V) outline: When switching to the Move Tool (V) and enabling the option to always view outlines/transform controls, it shows where the frame is supposed to be.
⚬ Treated as a standard empty group: The Layers panel creates Frame 1 as a folder/group layer.
⚬ Missing Transform controls: Selecting Frame 1 in the Properties panel only displays alignment options (Alinear y distribuir) and quick actions (Desagrupar capas / Convertir en objeto inteligente), completely omitting the Transformar (An, Al, X, Y) fields.
